content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Unsupervised anomaly detection methods such as isolation forest and one-class SVM can be applied to industrial data streams without labelled attack examples, with anomaly scores serving as control-chart statistics for alarm generation.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08489","field":"abstract","quote":"anomaly scorers whose output feeds threshold-based alarms"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-08490","field":"abstract","quote":"One-class support vector machines produce a real-valued decision score"}]},{"text":"Concept drift in normal operation due to seasonal variation and production-mix changes can be monitored and mitigated using a secondary drift detector such as the Page–Hinkley test, enabling incremental model updates without full retraining.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08494","field":"abstract","quote":"concept drift: the statistical properties of normal operation change over months due to seasonal variation"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-08494","field":"abstract","quote":"secondary drift monitor based on the Page–Hinkley test applied to the score distribution's empirical mean and variance"}]},{"text":"Lightweight incremental learning procedures can re-weight anomaly detectors using recent in-control samples, enabling fast recalibration on resource-constrained edge devices without retraining from scratch.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08494","field":"abstract","quote":"lightweight incremental update procedure re-weights the forest using recent in-control samples without full retraining"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-08490","field":"abstract","quote":"discusses feasibility for edge deployment"}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The records directly address the core challenge: building unsupervised anomaly detection models for industrial operational technology without labelled attack data [SYN-PUB-08494, SYN-PUB-08490], handling concept drift from normal operational changes [SYN-PUB-08494], and deploying on edge devices with limited computational resources [SYN-PUB-08490]."}
